vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: tech-news-digest
Version: 3.16.0

The tech-news-digest skill bundle is a well-structured and documented news aggregation system. It uses a series of Python scripts to fetch, merge, and score data from RSS feeds, Twitter/X, GitHub, Reddit, and web search APIs. While the scripts utilize high-risk capabilities such as shell execution (via subprocess for orchestration and email delivery) and extensive network access, these actions are strictly aligned with the stated purpose. The code demonstrates security awareness by including input sanitization (e.g., URL scheme validation in fetch-rss.py), explicit instructions to the agent to avoid shell interpolation of untrusted content (in digest-prompt.md), and the use of temporary files for sensitive operations like PDF generation and email construction.

llm.summary: This appears to be a real tech-news digest skill, but it needs review because it can run scheduled shell workflows, use credentials, fetch broad configurable URLs, and send results externally with incomplete safeguards.

dimensions.detail: Outbound network access is purpose-aligned, but RSS and article enrichment can request configured or feed-provided URLs without private-address or redirect validation, and security notes understate egress by claiming no data is sent outside a fixed endpoint set.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not appear to auto-install packages itself, but documentation recommends pip install with unpinned lower-bound dependencies and broad natural-language install/scheduling examples that should require explicit user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime prompt tells agents to substitute placeholders directly into shell snippets and follow the workflow strictly; WORKSPACE, SKILL_DIR, EMAIL, EMAIL_FROM, SUBJECT, and delivery targets are not robustly validated or quoted in the prompt-level commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Scheduled cron use, archive writes, temp caches, message/email delivery, and 90-day archive deletion are documented, but they are persistent or state-changing behaviors that need clearer scoping, confirmation, and reversibility controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core capability is coherent with the stated digest purpose: collect RSS, Twitter/X, GitHub, Reddit, and web-search items, score them, archive them, and deliver Discord/email/PDF output. Crypto and YouTube/RSS coverage are broad but mostly disclosed in README/SKILL defaults.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use a dedicated workspace and virtual environment, provide least-privilege API tokens, avoid enabling GH_APP_KEY_FILE or gh CLI fallback unless needed, confirm every scheduled job and delivery destination, disable enrichment for untrusted feeds, and do not import source configs from parties you do not trust until private-network URL blocking and safer command construction are added.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Brave/Tavily/Twitter/GitHub tokens are used as authentication to declared providers; I did not find evidence that arbitrary environment credentials are exfiltrated, so this is downgraded from the scanner framing.
[PE3] expected: GitHub token use is purpose-aligned, but GH_APP_KEY_FILE can read an arbitrary private-key path and the gh CLI fallback uses the local credential store, conflicting with the claim that no files outside the workspace are accessed.
[P3] expected: Sending generated digests to Discord/email is a declared feature, not conversation-context exfiltration by itself; users still need to confirm exact recipients and channels.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The one-message install and scheduling examples are broad and do not document confirmation boundaries for installation, persistent jobs, or external delivery.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The digest prompt instructs archive deletion after 90 days and enrich-articles.py overwrites input by default when output is omitted; both are real data-loss risks without enough guardrails.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill requests shell execution, message delivery, file writes, network access, and credential use without a tight least-privilege declaration or structured launcher boundaries.
[RA2] expected: Cron scheduling is a documented feature rather than hidden persistence, but recurring external delivery should be user-approved and easy to disable.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: the security notes say no files outside the workspace are accessed and no data goes to other endpoints, but the implementation can use GH_APP_KEY_FILE/gh credentials and can fetch arbitrary configured/feed article domains.
[SDI-1] expected: Crypto and broader source categories are present, but they are visible in README examples, default topics, and source counts, so this is not a standalone security concern.
[SQP-3] expected: Language defaults are inconsistent between Chinese and English examples, but LANGUAGE is a runtime placeholder and this did not drive the verdict.
[T09] unexpected: The SSRF concern is supported: fetch-rss.py and enrich-articles.py call urlopen on configured or article-provided URLs without validating resolved IPs, private ranges, or redirect destinations.
[T09] unexpected: The shell-injection concern is supported at the prompt layer because placeholder substitution is shown inside shell commands, including unquoted paths and single-quoted email fields.
[T08] expected: The dependencies are established packages and optional, but requirements.txt uses lower bounds without hashes or a lock file.
[T01] unexpected: The fixed footer with project attribution and a repository link is disclosed in templates, but it is mandatory generated content rather than user-selected report text.
